Rashi on Chullin 102b:11:1.hebrew: לא תאכל הנפש עם הבשר זה אבר מן החי - דאבר חי מקרינן נפש, שאם יחתכנו אינו עושה חליפין, שלא ישוב עוד, כנפש הנטולה שאינה חוזרת. והכי משמע: "לא תאכל הנפש" בעודו "עם הבשר" — בעוד החיות עם הבשר:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:11:1.english: “You shall not eat the life with the flesh” — this is a limb from a living [animal] - For a living limb is called “life” [nefesh], because if one cuts it off it does not regenerate, [in] that it will not return again, like a life that is taken, which does not return. And this is what [the verse] means: “You shall not eat the life” while it is “with the flesh” — while the vitality is with the flesh:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:11:2.hebrew: ובשר בשדה - משמע שפירש ממקומו, זהו בשר מן החי, ו"טרפה" כמשמעו:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:11:2.english: And flesh in the field - [this] implies that it separated from its place — this is flesh from a living [animal] — and "tereifa" [is understood] according to its plain meaning:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:12:1.hebrew: וריש לקיש אמר לא תאכל הנפש עם הבשר זה אבר מן החי ובשר מן החי - והכי משמע: לא תאכל הנפש, ולא תאכל הבשר כל זמן שזה עם זה:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:12:1.english: And Reish Lakish says: "You shall not eat the life with the flesh" — this [is] a limb from a living [animal] and flesh from the living - And this is what [the verse] implies: You shall not eat the life, and you shall not eat the flesh as long as this [the life] is with this [the flesh]:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:13:1.hebrew: לר' יוחנן חייב שתים - דתרי לאוי איכא, ואע"ג דבחדא אכילה וחדא התראה אכלינהו, מיחייב תרתי:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:13:1.english: According to Rabbi Yochanan he is liable [for] two [sets of lashes] - because there are two prohibitions, and even though he ate them in one act of eating and [with] one warning, he is liable [for] two:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:13:2.hebrew: אלא אחת - דחד לאו הוא, וכיון דבחדא אכילה וחדא התראה וחד לאו הוא, חדא הוא דמיחייב; וכן כולן:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:13:2.english: Only one - Because it is a single negative prohibition, and since it was [done] in one act of eating, with one warning, and [under] one negative prohibition, he is liable for [only] one [set of lashes]; and the same [applies to] all of them:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:13:3.english: Everyone agrees [that] he is liable [for] two - for according to both this [master] and that [master], they [the two prohibitions] are derived from two [separate] verses:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:1:1.english: While it is alive, for any amount - Because of [the prohibition of] a limb from a living [animal]. Thus, we do not require an olive-bulk for it:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:1:2.hebrew: במיתתה בכזית - דבנבלה אכילה כתיבא, וכל אכילה בכזית, בר מאבר מן החי, דרבייה קרא וקפיד אאבר לחודיה:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:1:2.english: When dead, for an olive-bulk - for regarding a carcass, "eating" is written [in the verse], and every [prohibition of] "eating" [requires] an olive-bulk, except for a limb from a living [animal], which the verse included and was particular about the limb alone:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:1:3.hebrew: טמאה בין בחייה בין במיתתה בכל שהוא - חייב, דבריה היא ולא צריכה שיעור, כדתנן באלו הן הלוקין (מכות דף יג.): באוכל נמלה כל שהוא, שהוא חייב משום שהיא כברייתה; אלמא בריה אסורה בכל שהוא. אבל לאו דנבלה ליכא לחיובי משום בריה, דכשנבראת לא היה עליה שם נבלה; הלכך אלאו דנבלה לא מיחייב עד כזית. קתני מיהא בטהורה בחייה בכל שהוא:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:1:3.english: A non-kosher [bird], whether alive or dead, [one is liable] for any amount - [he is] liable, because it is a complete creature [beriyah] and does not require a [minimum] measure, as we learned in the Mishnah in [the chapter entitled] Eilu Hen HaLokin (Makkot 13a): regarding one who eats an ant of any size, that he is liable because it is in its [original] created state; thus, a complete creature is forbidden in any amount. However, [for] the prohibition of nevelah [an unslaughtered carcass] one cannot be held liable on account of [its being] a complete creature, because when it was created it did not have the status of nevelah upon it; therefore, for the prohibition of nevelah one is not liable until [he eats] an olive-bulk. At any rate, [the baraita] teaches regarding a kosher [bird] when alive, [that one is liable] for any amount:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:2:1.english: He took a bird - and it is [of a] kosher [species]:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:2:2.hebrew: רבי פוטר - מפרש ואזיל, דקסבר: אין אבר מן החי בשלימה, דלאו אבר מיקריא; ומיהו אי איכא כזית — הוה מיחייב, דלא גרע מבשר מן החי דמיחייב עלה בכזית, דהא נמי בשר הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:2:2.english: Rabbi exempts [him] - [The Gemara] goes on to explain that he holds [the prohibition of] a limb from a living [animal] does not apply to a whole [creature], since it is not called a "limb." However, if there is an olive-bulk [of meat], he would be liable, for it is no less [stringent] than flesh from a living [animal], for which one is liable for [eating] an olive-bulk, since this too is flesh:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:2:3.hebrew: ורבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון מחייב - דקסבר: שלימה — אין לך אבר מן החי גדול מזה, ובאבר לא בעינא כזית:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:2:3.english: And Rabbi Elazar bar Rabbi Shimon deems [him] liable - for he holds [that regarding] a whole [bird], there is no greater "limb from a living animal" than this, and for a limb we do not require an olive-bulk:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:2:4.hebrew: חנקה ואכלה - אין כאן אלא איסור נבלה, ואנבלה לא מיחייב משום בריה, וכזית בעינן:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:2:4.english: [If] he strangled it and ate it - There is only the prohibition of nevelah [an unslaughtered carcass] here, and for nevelah one is not liable on account of [its being a complete] creature, and [therefore] an olive-bulk is required:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:3:1.hebrew: לאברים עומדת - לנתחה עומדת, הלכך כל אבר ואבר שבה קרוי אבר בפני עצמו, ויש כאן משום אבר מן החי דמיחייב בכל דהו; ומיהו חדא הוא דמיחייב, דחדא התראה היא:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:3:1.english: [It] stands [to be divided] into limbs - It stands to be cut into pieces; therefore, each and every limb in it is called a limb on its own, and there is [a prohibition] here on account of a limb from a living creature, for which one is liable for any minimal amount; however, he is liable for [only] one [transgression], since it is [only] one warning:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:3:2.hebrew: לאו לאברים עומדת - עד שתשחט, ואין כאן שם אבר אא"כ הפרישו, אבל דכ"ע לאבר לא בעינן כזית, כדקתני ק"ו: "על אבר ממנה חייב", ולא פליג רבי:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:3:2.english: [It] does not stand [to be divided] into limbs - until it is slaughtered, and there is no status of a limb here unless one separated it [from the body]; however, according to everyone, for a limb we do not require an olive-bulk, as it teaches [by] an a fortiori inference: "for a limb from it, he is liable," and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] does not disagree:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:4:1.hebrew: במשהו בשר - הא דקתני "שאין בו כזית", כשאין בו כזית בשר, אלא משהו, וגידין ועצמות משלימין לכזית:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:4:1.english: With a small amount of meat - That which [the baraita] teaches, "that does not contain an olive-bulk," [means] when it does not contain an olive-bulk of meat, but rather a small amount, and sinews and bones complete [it] to an olive-bulk:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:5:1.english: Is there any [such] thing - a bird so scrawny:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:5:2.hebrew: דבכוליה ליכא כזית בשר - והוא גדול שבאחת מאבריו איכא כזית במשהו בשר, וגידין ועצמות משלימין? דקתני "על אבר ממנה חייב", ואמרת דבכזית עסקינן, ורישא קתני "שאין בו כזית", ומוקמינן דליכא כזית בשר:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:5:2.english: That in its entire [body] there is not an olive-bulk of meat - And is it [so] large that in one of its limbs there is an olive-bulk through a small amount of meat, with sinews and bones completing [the measure]? For [the Mishnah] teaches, "For a limb from it, he is liable," and you said that we are dealing with [a limb containing] an olive-bulk, whereas the first clause teaches, "that does not have an olive-bulk in it," and we established [that it means] that there is not an olive-bulk of meat:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:6:1.hebrew: קלניתא עוף טמא הוא - ונהי דליכא איסור נבלה בפחות מכזית, איסור טמא מיהא איכא, דבריה היא, דאמר רב: טמאה בין בחייה ובין במיתתה בכל שהוא:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:6:1.english: A kelanita is a non-kosher bird - And even though there is no prohibition of neveilah [an unslaughtered carcass] for [eating] less than an olive-bulk, there is nonetheless the prohibition of a non-kosher [creature], since it is a [whole] creature, as Rav said: [Regarding] a non-kosher [bird], whether [eaten] while alive or dead, [one is liable] for any amount.

Rashi on Chullin 102b:6:2.english: Similar to a kelanita - A kosher bird that is scrawny like a kelanita:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:7:1.hebrew: את"ל - אם תמצא באחד מדבריו של רבי בעלמא דאית ליה מחשבת אוכלין, אם חישב לאוכלן כענין זה:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:7:1.english: If you say - If you find in one of the statements of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] elsewhere that he holds [the principle of] thought regarding food, [then] if he thought to eat them in this manner:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:7:2.english: Is considered thought - and we follow it:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:7:3.english: [If] he thought to eat it - [referring to] this bird that does not contain an olive-bulk:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:7:4.hebrew: אבר אבר - גלי אדעתיה דלאברים עומדת, וכי אכלה שלימה נמי אבר קרינא ביה:
Rashi on Chullin 102b:7:4.english: Limb by limb - He has revealed his intention that it stands [to be divided] into limbs, and when he eats it whole as well, we call it a limb:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:8:1.english: [If] another [person] ate it, he would not be liable - because it is not called a limb, to make one liable for [eating] any amount of it:

Rashi on Chullin 102b:9:1.english: To eat it [when] dead - for he revealed his intent that during its lifetime it does not stand [to be divided] into limbs:

Tosafot on Chullin 102b:11:1.hebrew: ובשר בשדה טרפה זה בשר מן החי - מדכתיב "בשדה" דריש, דמשמע שפירש ממקומו; ואף על גב דאצטריך לבשר שיצא חוץ ממחיצתו, כדאמר בפ' בהמה המקשה (לעיל חולין דף סח:), כולהו דריש מיניה:
Tosafot on Chullin 102b:11:1.english: “And flesh that is torn in the field” — this is flesh from the living - [Rabbi Yoḥanan] expounds [this] from that which is written “in the field,” which implies that it separated from its place. And even though [this word] is needed for flesh that went outside its partition — as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Behemah HaMaksheh (above, Chullin 68b) — he expounds all of them from it:

Tosafot on Chullin 102b:13:1.hebrew: אכל אבר מן החי ובשר מן החי לר' יוחנן חייב שתים - ואע"ג דאין לוקין על לאו שבכללות, ה"מ היכא דלא מפרש בקרא, כגון (שמות יב) "אל תאכלו כי אם צלי אש", ו"מכל אשר יעשה מגפן היין" (במדבר ו); אבל "ובשר בשדה טרפה", דמפרשינן בשר וטריפה, לא חשיב ליה לאו שבכללות, כמו נא ומבושל וחרצן וזג דמפרשי בקרא, לקי, וכגון אלמנה וגרושה דלקי לכ"ע:
Tosafot on Chullin 102b:13:1.english: If one ate a limb from a living [animal] and flesh from the living, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan he is liable [to receive] two [sets of lashes] - And even though one does not receive lashes for a generalized prohibition [i.e., a single negative commandment encompassing multiple prohibitions], that applies only where [each item] is not specified in the verse, such as (Exodus 12[:9]) "Do not eat [of it ...] except roasted in fire," and "from anything that is made of the grapevine" (Numbers 6[:4]). However, [regarding] "and flesh in the field, a tereifa" [Exodus 22:30], since we interpret [it as referring explicitly to] flesh [from the living] and tereifa, it is not considered a generalized prohibition; [rather, it is] like "raw" and "boiled," and "grape seed" and "grape skin," which are specified in the verse [and for which] one receives lashes, and like "a widow and a divorcee" [Leviticus 21:14], for which one receives lashes according to everyone:

Tosafot on Chullin 102b:13:2.hebrew: לרבי יוחנן אינו חייב אלא אחת - משום דמחד קרא נפקי. ואף על גב דאנא ומבושל לקי שתים, שאני התם דכתיב בוי"ו "ובשל", דקאי א"אל תאכלו"; והכא נמי, אי הוה כתיב "בשדה וטרפה לא תאכלו", היה לוקה שתים לרבי יוחנן משום בשר מן החי ובשר מן הטריפה:
Tosafot on Chullin 102b:13:2.english: According to Rabbi Yoḥanan he is liable [to receive] only one [set of lashes] - Because they [both] derive from one verse. And even though for "raw" and "boiled" [of the Paschal lamb] one receives two [sets of lashes], it is different there, because it is written with a vav — "u'vashel" [meaning "and boiled"] — which refers back to "do not eat" [creating two separate prohibitions]. And here too, if it were written "in the field and a tereifah you shall not eat," he would receive two [sets of lashes] according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, on account of flesh from a living [animal] and flesh from a tereifah:

Tosafot on Chullin 102b:1:1.hebrew: אכל צפור כו' הכא נמי במשהו בשר גידים ועצמות - ובין הכל צריך שיהא כזית, ולא הוי כמשהו דסיפא, דהוי בריה והוי משהו ממש:
Tosafot on Chullin 102b:1:1.english: [If one] ate a bird, etc. Here also [it is referring to] a small amount of meat, sinews, and bones - And altogether there must be an olive-bulk, and it is not like the "any amount" of the latter clause, which is a [whole] creature and is literally any amount:

Tosafot on Chullin 102b:2:1.hebrew: שאין בו כזית ואכלו רבי פוטר - פי' בקונטרס דקסבר דאין אבר מן החי בשלימה, ומיהו אי איכא כזית הוה מחייב, דלא גרע מבשר מן החי דמחייב בכזית, דהא נמי בשר הוא. וקשה לפירושו, דאמר בסמוך: אכל אבר מן החי ובשר מן הטרפה, רבי יוחנן אמר חייב שתים, וריש לקיש אמר אינו חייב אלא אחת; ומוקי לה בבהמה אחת ונטרפה עם יציאת רובה, וקסבר ר"ל דלאו לאברים עומדת, ולא אתי איסור אבר מן החי וחייל אאיסור טרפה. והשתא, מ"מ ליחייב שתים משום טרפה ובשר מן החי דקאתו בהדי הדדי! ויש לדחות: כגון שאין באבר זה כזית בשר, דלא מיחייב משום בשר מן החי, והא דחייב משום טרפה — היינו כשלקח בשר מטרפה אחרת והשלים לכזית. ודוחק הוא. ועוד, דא"כ, אמאי לא חייל עליה איסור אבר מן החי, כיון דליכא מטרפה אלא חצי שיעור? דבפ' בתרא דיומא (דף עג:) ופרק ג' דשבועות (דף כא:) תניא: שבועה שלא אוכל טרפות ונבלות שקצים ורמשים, חייב; ומוקי לה ר"ל במפרש חצי שיעור. אלמא, אע"ג דלא חייל איסור שבועה אכזית משום דמושבע ועומד הוא, מ"מ חייל אחצי כזית. ונראה לפרש: כי היכי דלאו לאברים עומדת, הכי נמי לאו לחתיכת בשר עומדת, והא דנקט צפור שאין בו כזית — לרבותא דרבי אלעזר נקט, דאפ"ה מחייב. ועוד נראה לר"י, דאפילו למ"ד לאברים עומדת, מודה דלאו לחתיכת בשר עומדת בחייה; דאמר ר' יוחנן בסמוך: אכל חלב מן החי מן הטרפה, חייב שלשה, ומוקי לה בנטרפה עם יציאת רובה ובהמה לאברים עומדת, דאתי איסור טרפה וחלב ואבר מן החי בהדי הדדי. והשתא, אמאי נקט טרפה? בלאו טרפה איכא ג': אבר מן החי ובשר מן החי וחלב! אלא ודאי בהמה בחייה לאו לחתיכת בשר עומדת, ולא אתי וחייל על שאר איסורין:
Tosafot on Chullin 102b:2:1.english: That did not have an olive-bulk and he ate it, Rabbi exempts [him] - Rashi explained that [Rabbi] holds there is no [prohibition of] a limb from a living animal for a whole [creature]; however, if there were an olive-bulk he would be liable, for it is no less [stringent] than flesh from a living animal, for which one is liable for an olive-bulk, since this too is flesh. But his explanation is difficult, for [the Gemara] says shortly [below]: If one ate a limb from a living animal and flesh from a terefah, Rabbi Yochanan says he is liable for two [sets of lashes], and Reish Lakish says he is liable for only one. And [the Gemara] establishes this regarding a single animal that became a terefah upon the emergence of its majority, and Reish Lakish holds that [a living animal] does not stand [divided] into limbs, so the prohibition of a limb from a living animal does not come and take effect upon the prohibition of terefah. Now, in any case, let him be liable for two on account of terefah and flesh from a living animal, which come simultaneously! One could deflect [this by saying it is] a case where there is not an olive-bulk of flesh in this limb, so he is not liable on account of flesh from a living animal, and that which he is liable on account of terefah is when he took flesh from another terefah and completed [the measure] to an olive-bulk. But this is forced. And furthermore, if so, why does the prohibition of a limb from a living animal not take effect upon it, since there is only half a measure from the terefah? For in the last chapter of Yoma (73b) and the third chapter of Shevuot (21b) it was taught: "[If one takes] an oath that I will not eat terefot, nevelot, abominations, or creeping things," he is liable; and Reish Lakish establishes it where he explicitly specifies half a measure. Thus we see that even though the prohibition of an oath does not take effect upon an olive-bulk because he is already under oath [from Sinai], nevertheless it takes effect upon half an olive-bulk. Therefore it appears [preferable] to explain: just as [a living animal] does not stand [divided] into limbs, so too it does not stand [divided] into pieces of flesh; and as for why [the baraita] mentioned a bird that does not have an olive-bulk — it mentioned [it] to show the novelty of Rabbi Elazar's [view], that even so he holds [him] liable. And furthermore, it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak that even according to the one who says [a living animal] stands [divided] into limbs, he agrees that it does not stand [divided] into pieces of flesh during its lifetime; for Rabbi Yochanan says shortly [below]: "If one ate chelev (forbidden fat) from a living [animal], from a terefah, he is liable for three," and [the Gemara] establishes it where it became a terefah upon the emergence of its majority and [holds that] an animal stands [divided] into limbs, so that the prohibitions of terefah, chelev, and a limb from a living animal come simultaneously. Now why did he mention terefah? Even without terefah there are three: a limb from a living animal, flesh from a living animal, and chelev! Rather, certainly an animal during its lifetime does not stand [divided] into pieces of flesh, and [that prohibition] does not come and take effect upon other prohibitions:
